retry_prompt:
Answer directly, no clarifying questions.

I post `NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL` on one vehicle, but the receiving vehicle never sees the payload variable. Walk through the message path and what to check.
text:
Here's the full message path for NODEMESSAGELOCAL and what to check at each stage.

Here's the full message path for NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL and what to check at each stage.

What NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL means

LOCAL means the message is dispatched only within the same node (process). It does not cross the network or inter-process transport. If vehicle A and vehicle B are separate nodes/processes, a LOCAL message posted on A will never reach B by design — that's the root cause in most cases.

Message path walkthrough
poster (Vehicle A)
  └─ postMessage(NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL, payload)
       └─ message bus (in-process only)
            └─ subscribers on the SAME node
                 ✗ Vehicle B (different node) — never receives this
What to check, in order

1. Is the receiving vehicle actually on the same node? This is the most common mistake. LOCAL is scoped to one process/node. If the two vehicles run as separate processes or on separate machines, switch to NODE_MESSAGE (inter-node, same machine) or NODE_MESSAGE_GLOBAL / the appropriate cross-node variant.

2. Is the subscriber registered before the message is posted? Local messages are typically fire-and-forget with no queuing. If Vehicle B registers its listener after the post, it misses it. Check initialization order.

3. Is the subscriber registered on the correct message type/ID? Confirm the receiving vehicle is subscribed to exactly NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL with the same message ID or topic string you're posting. A typo or mismatched enum value means the handler never fires.

4. Is the payload being read from the right field? Some frameworks wrap the payload in a message object (e.g., msg.data, msg.payload, event.content). Confirm the receiver is unpacking the correct field, not reading a top-level property of the message envelope.

5. Is the subscriber on the same thread/executor? If the framework dispatches local messages on a specific thread or executor loop, a subscriber bound to a different thread context may silently not fire. Check if you need to register on the main loop or a shared executor.

6. Are there any filtering conditions on the subscription? Some implementations let you attach source filters (vehicle ID, component ID) to subscriptions. If Vehicle B filters by source and Vehicle A's ID doesn't match, it drops the message silently.

Quick diagnostic

Add a logging subscriber on the same node as the poster, subscribed to the same message. If that fires but Vehicle B still doesn't receive it, the problem is definitively the node boundary — swap the message type. If even the logging subscriber doesn't fire, the post itself is failing (wrong ID, bad registration, or a threading issue).
